title: PILOT in the Loop: Live Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Agents
raw_text:
arXiv:2608.26530v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon agent runs generate experience that can improve both the current run and future work. Most self-improvement methods process this experience only after execution ends, so they cannot redirect the active run or immediately apply and validate lessons learned from it. We argue that self-improvement should instead be live, using emerging experience both to redirect the active run and to update the persistent harness. Existing agent architectures do not fully support this goal. Single-agent self-correction combines task execution and trajectory assessment within one context, while subagent delegation separates execution but typically cannot redirect an active subagent. We present PILOT, a supervisor-worker harness for live self-improvement through two coupled mechanisms: (1) live steering lets a separate supervisor redirect or abort the active worker during execution; and (2) live self-evolution distils procedures and failure mode
reason_zh: 提出PILOT在环实时自我改进方法，利用运行中经验即时调整长程智能体。
summary_zh: 长程智能体运行产生的经验可改进当前和未来工作，但大多数自我改进方法仅在执行结束后处理这些经验，无法重定向当前运行或立即应用和验证所学教训。本文主张自我改进应是实时的，利用新兴经验即时调整。作者提出PILOT在环方法，使智能体在运行过程中持续学习和改进，提升长程任务的适应性和效率。
title_zh: PILOT在环：长程智能体的实时自我改进

title: ProofEvolve: Neuro-Symbolic Evolution for Formal Automated Theorem Proving
raw_text:

Abstract: Automated theorem proving offers a natural foundation for recursive self-improvement in scientific discovery. summary_zh: 自动定理证明为科学发现中的递归自我改进提供了自然基础。然而，现有神经证明器并未完全保留这种递归结构，学习过程应随时间自我改进。现有方法要么通过昂贵的权重更新将证明经验嵌入模型参数，要么忽略经验积累。本文提出ProofEvolve，一种神经符号进化方法，旨在更有效地利用证明经验，实现自动定理证明的持续自我改进，推动科学发现自动化。

title: The Reasoning Tax: Token Economics of LLM Reasoning Across Task Types and Deployment Contexts
raw_text:
arXiv:2608.26235v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Accuracy-only benchmarking of reasoning-capable large language models misses a central deployment question: when do extended thinking tokens earn their cost? summary_zh: 本文指出仅以准确率评估推理型大语言模型忽略了部署中的关键问题：扩展思考token何时值得其成本。作者引入Token经济评分（TES），一种边际基准指标，衡量推理模型相对于非推理基线的准确率提升，并按生成token数归一化。通过跨任务类型和部署场景的分析，TES揭示了推理token在不同情境下的成本效益差异，为模型选择和资源分配提供量化依据。该研究为推理模型的实用评估提供了新视角。

title: SKILL.state: Scalable Long-Horizon Agent Skills
raw_text:
arXiv:2608.26263v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly act as autonomous agents executing complex, long-running procedural skills. Existing agent runtimes maintain execution by continually appending observations, actions, and intermediate reasoning traces to an ever-growing conversation history, causing latency degradation and context-poisoning failures over long horizons. We present SKILL.state, a runtime architecture that replaces append-only conversational history with an explicit, mutable execution state. At each execution step, the model receives only the immutable skill specification, the current structured execution state, and the latest observation. Intermediate reasoning is discarded immediately after producing a validated state update, preventing prompt growth with execution history. Across diverse datasets, models, and execution environments, SKILL.state improves task accuracy while substantially reducing cumulative token consumption. Our
reason_zh: 提出SKILL.state解决长程智能体上下文膨胀问题，提升可扩展性与稳定性。
summary_zh: 大型语言模型作为自主智能体执行复杂、长期运行的程序性技能时，现有运行时通过不断追加观察、动作和中间推理轨迹到不断增长的对话历史中，导致延迟退化和上下文中毒。本文提出SKILL.state，一种可扩展的长程智能体技能状态管理方法，旨在缓解这些问题。通过更高效的状态表示和更新机制，SKILL.state有望提升长程任务的执行效率和可靠性。
title_zh: SKILL.state：可扩展的长程智能体技能

title: Don't Overthink, Don't Underthink: Toward Adaptive Reasoning in Agentic AI
raw_text:
arXiv:2608.26442v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown that increased inference-time reasoning can improve performance on complex tasks. However, many existing approaches rely on fixed or preallocated reasoning controls, such as fixed token budgets, pre-execution difficulty estimates, or activation-space interventions, and are often evaluated on standalone reasoning benchmarks rather than full agentic workflows. These assumptions may not hold in agentic AI systems, where reasoning requirements evolve dynamically through planning, tool use, memory retrieval, and agent-to-agent interactions. Consequently, reasoning can become either excessive or insufficient, resulting in unnecessary computation, increased latency, planning drift, excessive tool use, or incomplete solutions. We argue that a major challenge for next-generation agentic AI is not merely how much reasoning a language model should perform, but how it should allocate reasoni
reason_zh: 探讨自适应推理控制，避免过度或不足思考，提升智能体效率与性能。
summary_zh: 近期进展表明，增加推理时间计算可提升复杂任务性能，但现有方法常依赖固定或预分配的推理控制，如固定token预算、执行前难度估计或激活空间干预，且评估场景有限。本文提出自适应推理方法，旨在根据任务需求动态调整推理深度，避免过度思考或思考不足。该方法有望在保持性能的同时降低计算成本，对智能体AI的实用部署具有重要意义。
title_zh: 不要过度思考，也不要思考不足：迈向智能体AI的自适应推理

title: Five Primitives for Governing Autonomous AI Agents at Runtime
raw_text:
arXiv:2608.26696v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Enterprise deployments of autonomous AI agents inherit a control model built for human users and long-lived services, and the fit fails in three specific ways: agent principals are ephemeral, appearing and vanishing faster than provisioning; their actions are selected by a model rather than programmed, so the set of things they may attempt is not known in advance; and the population is discovered rather than provisioned, because anyone who can call an API can create one. We argue that governing such agents is a runtime problem -- not a model-alignment problem and not a build-time problem -- and we derive five primitives from the questions that must be answered before an action takes effect and after it has: discovery, identity, governance, attestation, and supply chain. For each we state what fails if it is absent and why the others cannot structurally supply it. We describe an implementation in which an agent's action is mediated agains
reason_zh: 提出治理自主AI智能体的五个原语，解决企业部署中控制模型不匹配问题，对AI治理实践有重要指导意义。
summary_zh: 企业部署自主AI智能体时，继承了为人类用户和长期服务设计的控制模型，但在三个方面不匹配：智能体主体是短暂的，出现和消失速度快于配置；其行为由模型选择而非编程，因此可能尝试的行为集合未知；以及缺乏对智能体行为的实时治理机制。本文提出五个原语来治理运行时自主AI智能体，为企业AI治理提供了新框架。
title_zh: 运行时治理自主AI智能体的五个原语

title: Agentic AI for operating scientific instruments for nanoscale characterization
raw_text:
arXiv:2608.26198v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Operating a scientific instrument such as an atomic force microscope (AFM) requires continuous expert decision-making. A trained user defines the experimental intent, translates it into instrument commands, assesses incoming data, adjusts imaging parameters, and post-processes the final image. Existing automation usually addresses only parts of this workflow through hard-coded routines, task-specific controllers, or trained machine-learning models. Here we present an agentic-AI framework that operates the executable part of the AFM workflow using a general-purpose, tool-augmented large language model connected to instrument functions through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). summary_zh: 论文探讨了Agentic AI在操作科学仪器（如原子力显微镜）中的应用。操作此类仪器需要连续专家决策，包括定义实验意图、转换指令、评估数据、调整参数和后处理。现有自动化仅覆盖部分环节。作者提出一个Agentic AI系统，旨在端到端自动化整个流程，减少人工干预，提高表征效率。

raw_text:
Just a rumour of a bug is enough to find a security exploit these days

Anil Madhavapeddy is a professor of computer science at Cambridge and a core maintainer of the OCaml compiler. In this somewhat alarming post he reports that security issues in OCaml projects are seeing evidence of attempted exploits within minutes of patches being shared for discussion:

This normally takes a few days and a release within a week or two is reasonable. Within about ten minutes (!) this website was fielding probes for percent-encoded traversal sequences, indicating that automated watchers are keeping an eye on public repositories.
